18	The Defendants contend that the Complaint should be dismissed in its entirety for failure to comply with the 2004 Agreement’s dispute resolution and mediation clause. L.P./Inc. Mot. to Dismiss at 12-13. The clause provides that “[a]ny dispute, controversy or claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement, or the breach, termination, or invalidity thereof shall first be referred by the parties to their senior-level executives for attempted resolution through good-faith negotiations.” Compl. Ex. A § 9.1 (emphasis added). Should negotiations fail, thirty days after making a written request to initiate those negotiations, “either Party may, by written notice to the other, require that the Dispute be referred to non-binding mediation administered by the American Arbitration Association.” Id. Skold responds that the language of the mediation clause is permissive (“either Party may ... require”) and also argues that, in any event, Inc. has waived its right to invoke the clause because it participated in litigation over the dispute in the cancellation action before the TTAB. 19	The dispute resolution clause in the 2004 Agreement contains two clauses, one of which is mandatory (the parties shall refer the matter to senior executives to attempt to negotiate a resolution) and the other which is permissive (the parties may refer the matter to nonbinding mediation). 20	L.P. and S.A., who are not parties to the 2004 Agreement, also contend that the dispute resolution clause requires their dismissal from this action. In essence, they urge this Court to accept the contention that a nonparty to an agreement should be permitted to force a signatory party to engage in negotiations pursuant to a permissive mediation clause in that agreement as a condition precedent to filing suit but cite no relevant case or statute in support of this contention. See United States v. Benish, 5 F.3d 20, 26 (3d Cir.1993) (rejecting a party’s claim where the party “provided] no legal support for his argument or any persuasive reason” for the court to find in his favor). The Court sees no persuasive reason to dismiss Skold’s entire Complaint based on this unsupported argument. Accordingly, the motion to dismiss the Complaint against L.P. and S.A. on this ground shall be denied.
21	Regarding Inc.: although Skold did fail to bring in a senior-level executive to try to resolve the dispute — as he was required to do under the dispute resolution provision — Inc.’s participation in the TTAB proceedings waived any rights it may have had to seek to have the parties’ executives negotiate an end to the dispute. See, e.g., LBL Skysystems (USA), Inc. v. APG-Am., Inc., No. 02-5379, 2005 WL 2140240, at *30 (E.D.Pa. Aug. 31, 2005) (holding that a “party that engages in discovery and files pretrial motions waives a contract’s alternative dispute resolution provision”); Smith v. IMG Worldwide, Inc., 360 F.Supp.2d 681, 687 (E.D.Pa.2005) (finding that a party’s engaging in motion practice and providing “substantial discovery” constituted waiver of contractual alternative dispute resolution provision).
22	Viewing the four years’ worth of docket entries in the TTAB action, the Court considers that Inc. did not file a motion to stay the TTAB proceedings pending executive-level negotiations and instead filed, inter alia, motions to dismiss, a protective order, multiple summary judgment motions (one of which was partially granted in its favor), and a final brief in preparation for trial. See, e.g., Sköld v. Galderma Labs., Inc., Cancellation No. 92052897, 2012 WL 5902083 (T.T.A.B. Nov. 8, 2012) (granting Inc.’s motion for partial summary judgment on Skold’s abandonment claim). See also generally Registrant’s Trial Brief, Sköld v. Galderma Labs., Inc., Cancellation No. 92052897 (T.T.A.B. Aug. 13, 2014), Docket No. 81. This four-year history of litigation in the cancellation action — from filing nearly through trial — is, on its face, inconsistent with the notion that Inc. was willing to engage in the good-faith executive-level negotiations required by the dispute resolution provision.
23	Moreover, the Court can look to the TTAB’s grant of partial summary judgment in favor of Inc. and dismissing Skold’s abandonment claim as a concrete example of an instance where Inc.’s conduct inconsistent with the dispute resolution clause caused prejudice to Skold, not to mention the expenditure of time, cost, and resources attendant to maintaining a multi-year trademark cancellation action. 12	International ACH and Wire Transactions If your Account receives incoming ACH transactions (either credits or debits) or wire transfers initiated from outside of the United States, both you and we are subject to the Operating Rules and Guidelines of the National Automated Clearing House Association (“NACHA”) or the rules of any wire transfer system involved, and the laws enforced by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (“OFAC”). Under such rules and laws, we may temporarily suspend processing of a transaction for greater scrutiny or verification against the OFAC list of blocked parties, which may result in delayed settlement, posting and/or availability of funds. If we determine there is a violation, or if we cannot satisfactorily resolve a suspected or potential violation, the subject funds will be blocked as required by law. If you believe you have adequate grounds to seek the return of any blocked funds, it is your sole responsibility to pursue the matter with the appropriate governmental authorities. Please see the OFAC website for procedures and form required to seek a release of blocked funds.

This MORTGAGE LOAN PURCHASE AGREEMENT, dated as of July 6, 2007,

(“EMC” or a “Mortgage Loan Seller”), MORGAN STANLEY MORTGAGE CAPITAL

Seller”, and together with EMC, the “Mortgage Loan Sellers”) and BEAR STEARNS ASSET
BACKED SECURITIES I LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (the “Purchaser”).

Upon the terms and subject to the conditions of this Agreement, each Mortgage
Loan Seller agrees to sell, and the Purchaser agrees to purchase, certain conventional, closed-
end, subprime, fixed rate and adjustable rate, first and second lien mortgage loans secured by
one- to four-family residences (collectively, the “Mortgage Loans”) as described herein. The
Purchaser intends to deposit the Mortgage Loans into a trust fund (the “Trust Fund”) and create
Morgan Stanley Structured Trust I 2007-1, Asset-Backed Certificates, Series 2007-1 (the
Certificates”), under a pooling and servicing agreement, to be dated as of June 1, 2007 (the
“Pooling and Servicing Agreement”), among the Purchaser, as depositor, Wells Fargo Bank,
National Association, as master servicer (in such capacity, the “Master Servicer’) and securities
administrator (in such capacity, the “Securities Administrator’) and Deutsche Bank National
Trust Company, as trustee (the ““Trustee”).

The Purchaser has filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the
“Commission”) a registration statement on Form S-3 (Number 333-131374) relating to its Asset-
Backed Certificates and the offering of certain series thereof (including certain classes of the
Certificates) from time to time in accordance with Rule 415 under the Securities Act of 1933, as
amended, and the rules and regulations of the Commission promulgated thereunder (the
“Securities Act”). Such registration statement, when it became effective under the Securities Act,
and the prospectus relating to the public offering of certain classes of the Certificates by the
Purchaser (the “Public Offering”), as each may be amended or supplemented from time to time
pursuant to the Securities Act or otherwise, are referred to herein as the “Registration Statement”
and the “Prospectus,” respectively. The “Free Writing Prospectus” shall mean the free writing
prospectus, dated June 29, 2007, relating to certain classes of the Certificates. The “Prospectus
Supplement” shall mean the final supplement, dated July 5, 2007, to the Prospectus, dated June
26, 2007, relating to certain classes of the Certificates. With respect to the Public Offering of
certain classes of the Certificates, Bear, Stearns & Co. Inc. (“Bear Stearns”) and the Purchaser
have entered into a terms agreement, dated as of June 29, 2007, to an underwriting agreement,
dated April 13, 2006 (together, the “Underwriting Agreement”) between Bear Stearns and the
. Purchaser.

terms used herein but not defined herein shall have the meanings specified in the Pooling and
Servicing Agreement. The following other terms are defined as follows: |

SECTION 2. Agreement to Purchase Mortgage Loans.

The Seller agrees to sell, and the Purchaser agrees to purchase, on a servicing
retained basis, Mortgage Loans having an aggregate Stated Principal Balance on the Cut-off Date
in an amount set forth on the Mortgage Loan Schedule, together with the related Mortgage Files
and all rights and obligations arising under the documents contained therein.

SECTION 3. Mortgage Schedule.

The Seller shall deliver the Mortgage Loan Schedule for the Mortgage Loans to
be purchased on the Closing Date to the Purchaser at least two (2) Business Days prior to the
Closing Date; provided, however, that the Seller shall not be responsible for any delays in the
delivery of the Mortgage Loan Schedule caused by changes to the Mortgage Loans made at the
Purchaser’s request, so long as the Seller delivers the Mortgage Loan Schedule within a
reasonable period of time after such changes are requested.

SECTION 4. Purchase Price.

The Purchase Price for the Mortgage Loans shall be equal to the Purchase Price
Percentage multiplied by the aggregate Stated Principal Balance of the Mortgage Loans listed on
the Mortgage Loan Schedule, after application of payments of principal due or received on or
before the Cut-off Date. The Purchase Price shall be paid to the Seller by wire transfer of
immediately available funds to an account designated by the Seller in writing.

The Purchaser shall be entitled to (1) all scheduled principal due after the Cut-off
Date, (2) all other recoveries of principal collected on or after the Cut-off Date, and (3) all
payments of interest on the Mortgage Loans that accrue from and after the Closing Date, net of
applicable Servicing Fees.

{"judgments": [
{"clause_id":"c079","reasoning_cat1":"Short and absolute ('complete, true and correct as of the Cut-off Date'); no ambiguous term.","reasoning_cat2":"It is introduced by 'With respect to each Mortgage Loan', so MSMCH appears to warrant Schedule data for EMC's loans too, which sits oddly with Section 8's narrow EMC warranty and with the Section 1/Exhibit 2 mismatch about what the Schedule contains.","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.40},
{"clause_id":"c080","reasoning_cat1":"'Any and all requirements of any federal, state or local law including, without limitation' followed by a list of named statutes is the classic general-plus-enumeration structure whose reach is arguable.","reasoning_cat2":"The same rep is repeated verbatim in Part B(C) of Exhibit F of the attached Underlying Agreement and overlaps Section 10(a)(3), producing layered but not contradictory coverage.","prob_cat1":0.30,"prob_cat2":0.22},
{"clause_id":"c081","reasoning_cat1":"'High Cost Loan or Covered Loan, as applicable' leaves the qualifier 'as applicable' doing unexplained work, and the second sentence restates the HOEPA limb already inside the High Cost Loan definition.","reasoning_cat2":"It duplicates the defined term High Cost Loan in Section 1 and the identical rep in Exhibit F Part A(O), so the overlap is redundant rather than inconsistent.","prob_cat1":0.27,"prob_cat2":0.21},
{"clause_id":"c082","reasoning_cat1":"A concrete, date-and-day-count rep with an express Schedule exception; nothing genuinely ambiguous.","reasoning_cat2":"'Delinquent' is undefined here and comes only from the PSA hook in Section 1, while the Underlying Agreement supplies its own definition.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.19},
{"clause_id":"c083","reasoning_cat1":"Standard no-defenses warranty, closed and specific.","reasoning_cat2":"Mirrors Exhibit F Part A(B) of the attached agreement; no conflict.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.09},
{"clause_id":"c084","reasoning_cat1":"'a generally acceptable insurer' and 'such other hazards as are customarily insured against' are open-textured standards.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Exhibit F Part A(C); no other provision contradicts it.","prob_cat1":0.21,"prob_cat2":0.10},
{"clause_id":"c085","reasoning_cat1":"Permitted-encumbrance clause (iv) is a catch-all ('other matters to which like properties are commonly subject') sitting against three enumerated specifics, an ejusdem generis question.","reasoning_cat2":"It is the reference point for clause (6)'s title-insurance exceptions and mirrors Exhibit F Part A(E); the structures line up.","prob_cat1":0.31,"prob_cat2":0.16},
{"clause_id":"c086","reasoning_cat1":"'have been duly and properly executed by other such related parties' is garbled — 'other' appears where 'all' was plainly meant, changing who executed.","reasoning_cat2":"Exhibit F Part A(F) carries the identical error, so the defect is inherited rather than contradicted elsewhere.","prob_cat1":0.30,"prob_cat2":0.14},
{"clause_id":"c087","reasoning_cat1":"Detailed and specific, though 'other generally acceptable form of policy or insurance acceptable to Fannie Mae or Freddie Mac' is an open standard.","reasoning_cat2":"It excepts 'Co-op Loan[s]', a term defined only in the attached Underlying Agreement and not in this one, and cross-refers to 'paragraph (4) of this Section 10' which is in subsection (b), not (a).","prob_cat1":0.21,"prob_cat2":0.29},
{"clause_id":"c088","reasoning_cat1":"Clear no-default rep; the exception cross-reference to 'paragraph (1) above' is accurate.","reasoning_cat2":"'Affiliates' is undefined in this Agreement and only defined in the attached Underlying Agreement, a small gap filled by the PSA hook.","prob_cat1":0.14,"prob_cat2":0.19},
{"clause_id":"c089","reasoning_cat1":"Concrete disbursement and cost rep; nothing to construe.","reasoning_cat2":"Matches Exhibit F Part A(I) of the attached agreement.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c090","reasoning_cat1":"Specific mechanics'-lien rep with a parenthetical about inchoate rights; tight drafting.","reasoning_cat2":"Matches Exhibit F Part A(J); no conflict.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c091","reasoning_cat1":"'customary and enforceable provisions such as to render the rights and remedies ... adequate' turns on two undefined evaluative words, 'customary' and 'adequate'.","reasoning_cat2":"Mirrors Exhibit F Part A(K); no inconsistency with other provisions.","prob_cat1":0.28,"prob_cat2":0.10},
{"clause_id":"c092","reasoning_cat1":"The rep states the provision is enforceable and then repeats that it is enforceable 'to the best of MSMCH's knowledge', an internal redundancy that muddles whether the rep is absolute or knowledge-qualified.","reasoning_cat2":"Exhibit F Part A(L) contains the same doubled formulation; no conflicting provision elsewhere.","prob_cat1":0.24,"prob_cat2":0.12},
{"clause_id":"c093","reasoning_cat1":"'in good repair' and 'undamaged ... so as to affect adversely the value' are evaluative but conventional; the last sentence flatly contradicts nothing.","reasoning_cat2":"Matches Exhibit F Part A(M); no conflict found.","prob_cat1":0.18,"prob_cat2":0.09},
{"clause_id":"c094","reasoning_cat1":"'taking into such facts as' is missing a word ('account'), and 'higher cost product designed for less creditworthy mortgagors' is a vague standard applied to the Originator's conduct.","reasoning_cat2":"Identical to Exhibit F Part A(N), which the Underlying Agreement deems automatically material; here no such deeming applies, a difference in effect.","prob_cat1":0.39,"prob_cat2":0.20},
{"clause_id":"c095","reasoning_cat1":"A bare '[Reserved]'; there is no text to construe.","reasoning_cat2":"Its numbering keeps the parallel with Exhibit F's lettered list, but a reserved slot cannot conflict with anything.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c096","reasoning_cat1":"Concrete list of charges with an escrow alternative; clear.","reasoning_cat2":"Matches Exhibit F Part A(P); the reference to leasehold payments sits oddly with the Section 1 Mortgage definition limited to fee simple estates.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.20},
{"clause_id":"c097","reasoning_cat1":"'approved by the issuer of the title insurer' is garbled (the issuer is the title insurer), and the rep both requires terms to be reflected in the Schedule and then repeats it 'if applicable'.","reasoning_cat2":"The Mortgage Loan Schedule fields listed in Section 1 and Exhibit 2 contain no field for modifications, so the promise that modification terms 'are reflected in the Mortgage Loan Schedule' has no home.","prob_cat1":0.28,"prob_cat2":0.28},
{"clause_id":"c098","reasoning_cat1":"A technical tax rep tied to a specific Code section; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Matches Exhibit F Part A(R); consistent with the REMIC structure contemplated by the recital.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.09},
{"clause_id":"c099","reasoning_cat1":"'Solely with respect to' followed by four named loan groups is an express limitation whose negative implication for all other loans is stark.","reasoning_cat2":"It sits inside subsection (b), which by its terms applies only to MSMCH Represented Mortgage Loans, yet Fremont and Accredited loans are not in that defined list — the ownership warranty's scope is genuinely uncertain.","prob_cat1":0.33,"prob_cat2":0.51},
{"clause_id":"c100","reasoning_cat1":"Concrete survey/zoning rep; nothing ambiguous.","reasoning_cat2":"Matches Exhibit F Part A(T); no conflict.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c101","reasoning_cat1":"Detailed appraisal rep; 'Qualified Appraiser' is capitalised but undefined in this Agreement.","reasoning_cat2":"It says the appraiser was 'duly appointed by MSMCH' although the loans were originated by third-party originators, and Qualified Appraiser is defined only in the attached Underlying Agreement as appointed by its Seller.","prob_cat1":0.26,"prob_cat2":0.33},
{"clause_id":"c102","reasoning_cat1":"'LTV' is used without definition anywhere in this Agreement, and it is unclear whether it means the Loan-to-Value Ratio or, for second liens, the CLTV.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 1 defines 'Value' and the Schedule fields use Loan-to-Value Ratio and CLTV, none of which is 'LTV', so the measure for second-lien loans is left open.","prob_cat1":0.34,"prob_cat2":0.31},
{"clause_id":"c103","reasoning_cat1":"Long but concrete, with dated tiers and a modification proviso; the only softness is 'permitted pursuant to federal, state and local law'.","reasoning_cat2":"It promises MSMCH will enforce prepayment penalties 'for the benefit of the Purchaser' although servicing is performed by others under the Pooling and Servicing Agreement, a practical mismatch.","prob_cat1":0.19,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c104","reasoning_cat1":"The parenthetical list omits a comma ('accident unemployment') but the meaning is not altered.","reasoning_cat2":"Matches Exhibit F Part A(X); no conflict.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c105","reasoning_cat1":"A single dated, absolute rep; nothing to construe.","reasoning_cat2":"Matches Exhibit F Part A(Y); consistent.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c106","reasoning_cat1":"'the representations and warranties set forth above shall be deemed to be made by the related Mortgage Loan Seller' introduces a party ('related Mortgage Loan Seller') different from MSMCH, the only representor in Section 10.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 8 gives EMC no loan-level warranties to re-make on substitution, and Replacement Mortgage Loan has no stated eligibility criteria, so the deeming provision has uncertain content.","prob_cat1":0.24,"prob_cat2":0.34},
{"clause_id":"c107","reasoning_cat1":"The notice trigger covers 'any representation or warranty of MSMCH set forth in this Section 10' but the remedy and the exclusivity clause speak only of MSMCH Represented Mortgage Loans, and 'sole and exclusive remedy under this Agreement or otherwise' is sweeping.","reasoning_cat2":"It clashes with Section 10(a) (reps as to 'each Mortgage Loan'), with Section 19 (which locates the cure/purchase obligations in 'Sections 5 and 7'), and with Section 21's unqualified survival of all representations.","prob_cat1":0.47,"prob_cat2":0.62},
{"clause_id":"c108","reasoning_cat1":"It refers to 'a representation or warranty set forth in this Section 10 made by Accredited', but Accredited makes no representations in Section 10 at all.","reasoning_cat2":"The Accredited reps live in the Accredited Assignment, Assumption and Recognition Agreement (Exhibit 8, itself only a tab reference), and Accredited loans are outside the MSMCH Represented Mortgage Loans definition that governs the preceding paragraph.","prob_cat1":0.41,"prob_cat2":0.55},
{"clause_id":"c109","reasoning_cat1":"It defines when a cause of action 'shall accrue' by reference to discovery and failure to cure, a formulation whose legal effect (limitations period versus condition precedent) is contestable on its own words.","reasoning_cat2":"It sits against the Section 10 sole-remedy paragraph and Section 21's survival clause, and applies only to 'MSMCH Represented Mortgage Loans' though the reps in Section 10(a) are broader.","prob_cat1":0.38,"prob_cat2":0.44},
{"clause_id":"c110","reasoning_cat1":"A short assignment of two named agreements; 'BSABS I' is used as a shorthand never defined in the Agreement, and clause (a) omits any date.","reasoning_cat2":"Sections 2(a), 2(c) and 20 all treat 'Section 11' as containing the closing conditions, which it plainly does not, and the table of contents gives this section a different title again.","prob_cat1":0.24,"prob_cat2":0.55},
{"clause_id":"c111","reasoning_cat1":"'[Reserved]' has no content to construe.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 19 nevertheless preserves for the Purchaser 'the benefits set forth in Sections 12, 14 and 18', so an operative provision points at an empty section.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.42},
{"clause_id":"c112","reasoning_cat1":"Short introductory clause fixing the speaking dates; nothing ambiguous.","reasoning_cat2":"Parallel to Sections 7 and 9; consistent.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c113","reasoning_cat1":"Boilerplate organization rep with materiality carve-out.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the preamble's description of the Purchaser as a Delaware LLC.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c114","reasoning_cat1":"One-line power rep; nothing to construe.","reasoning_cat2":"Mirrors Sections 7(b) and 9(b).","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c115","reasoning_cat1":"Standard no-conflict rep; the trailing 'or thereby' has no antecedent, a harmless residue.","reasoning_cat2":"Parallel to Sections 7(c) and 9(c); no conflict.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c116","reasoning_cat1":"Standard no-consent rep; 'or thereby' again lacks an antecedent but nothing turns on it.","reasoning_cat2":"Parallel to Sections 7(d) and 9(d).","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c117","reasoning_cat1":"Standard enforceability rep with creditor-rights qualification.","reasoning_cat2":"Mirrors Sections 7(e) and 9(e).","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c118","reasoning_cat1":"Standard no-litigation rep; the 'in the judgment of the Purchaser' limb is subjective but conventional.","reasoning_cat2":"Parallel to Sections 7(f) and 9(f).","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c119","reasoning_cat1":"Condition (2)(iv) contains a stray 'otherwise' and condition (3) refers to 'the Underwriting Agreement and the Purchase Agreement', the latter never defined.","reasoning_cat2":"Sections 2(a), 2(c) and 20 all cite 'Section 11' rather than this section for the closing conditions, and Section 7(g) claims 'Mortgage Loan Seller's Information' is defined in Section 14(a), which it is not.","prob_cat1":0.31,"prob_cat2":0.52},
{"clause_id":"c120","reasoning_cat1":"A clear, closed list of seller-side closing conditions; the drafting is unremarkable.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 20(c) permits a seller to terminate for failure of 'the conditions ... set forth under Section 11(b)', which points to the wrong section entirely.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.42},
{"clause_id":"c121","reasoning_cat1":"'shall pay fees and expenses as previously agreed' names neither the fees, the expenses, nor the agreement, leaving the obligation without ascertainable content.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 29 declares this Agreement the entire agreement and supersedes 'all prior and contemporaneous agreements', which would erase the very prior agreement this section relies on; Section 20 separately allocates expenses on termination.","prob_cat1":0.46,"prob_cat2":0.53},
{"clause_id":"c122","reasoning_cat1":"The first two sentences are near-identical duplicates, and the section is phrased as prediction ('Deloitte & Touche LLP will review') rather than obligation, leaving unclear who is bound.","reasoning_cat2":"It refers to letters 'required of them under the Underwriting Agreement', a document to which the Mortgage Loan Sellers are not parties, and to Schedule A of the offering documents rather than Schedule A hereto.","prob_cat1":0.28,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c123","reasoning_cat1":"'[Reserved]' has no content to construe.","reasoning_cat2":"Unlike Section 12, no other provision cross-refers to Section 17.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.10},

{"judgments": [
{"clause_id":"c139","reasoning_cat1":"A clear naming clause; the only oddity is that EMC is styled 'Purchaser' here and 'Mortgage Loan Seller' in the principal agreement.","reasoning_cat2":"The principal agreement's definition of 'Underlying EMC Purchase Agreement' describes this document as being 'between EMC and MSMCH', but the Seller here is Morgan Stanley Mortgage Capital Inc., a different entity from Morgan Stanley Mortgage Capital Holdings LLC.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.44},
{"clause_id":"c140","reasoning_cat1":"Conventional whereas clauses defining Mortgage Loans, Originator and Purchase Date; 'certain conventional fixed and adjustable rate' loans is loose but the Schedule fixes the pool.","reasoning_cat2":"The third recital says each loan is secured by an instrument 'creating a first or second lien', while the operative Mortgage definition says the instrument 'creates a first lien on the Mortgaged Property' — a recital/operative divergence.","prob_cat1":0.14,"prob_cat2":0.34},
{"clause_id":"c141","reasoning_cat1":"A one-line definitional preamble; nothing to construe.","reasoning_cat2":"Unlike the principal agreement, it supplies no fallback source for undefined capitalised terms such as 'Underwriting Guidelines' used in the CLTV definition.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.16},
{"clause_id":"c142","reasoning_cat1":"'accepted mortgage servicing practices of prudent mortgage lending institutions' is a circular and open-textured standard.","reasoning_cat2":"The defined term does not appear in any operative provision of the Agreement, which sells the loans servicing-retained under existing Servicing Agreements.","prob_cat1":0.23,"prob_cat2":0.26},

{"clause_id":"c144","reasoning_cat1":"Standard control-based Affiliate definition with a self-contained gloss on 'control'.","reasoning_cat2":"Used in Subsection 8.02 and Exhibit F consistently; the principal agreement uses 'Affiliates' without defining it.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.11},

{"clause_id":"c234","reasoning_cat1":"'the principal balance ... at the Cut-off Date after giving effect to payments of principal due on or before such date' leaves 'such date' ambiguous between the Cut-off Date and the date of determination.","reasoning_cat2":"Stated Principal Balance drives both the Purchase Price in Section 4 and the Repurchase Price, so the ambiguity has real consequences.","prob_cat1":0.29,"prob_cat2":0.23},

{"clause_id":"c243","reasoning_cat1":"It states the loans were sold 'servicing retained' and then assigns every Servicing Agreement to the Purchaser with the Servicers servicing 'for the Purchaser', which is in tension with the retained-servicing label.","reasoning_cat2":"It refers to 'the Mortgage Loan Schedule attached as Exhibit C hereto' when the Schedule is Exhibit B and Exhibit C holds the agreements, and Subsection 6.01 excepts the Servicing Rights from the conveyance.","prob_cat1":0.35,"prob_cat2":0.42},

{"clause_id":"c246","reasoning_cat1":"'The consummation of the transactions ... are' is a subject-verb slip, and 'ordinary course of business' is an evaluative standard.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the sale-treatment provisions in Subsections 6.02 and 8.01(g).","prob_cat1":0.17,"prob_cat2":0.08},

{"clause_id":"c249","reasoning_cat1":"'does not believe, nor does it have any reason or cause to believe, that it cannot perform' is a double-negative, wholly subjective formulation whose content is hard to pin down.","reasoning_cat2":"It overlaps the more objective authority and enforceability reps in 8.01(a) without conflicting with them.","prob_cat1":0.30,"prob_cat2":0.11},

{"clause_id":"c251","reasoning_cat1":"Several timing rules pull against each other — action 'within 120 days' of discovery, repurchase if the breach 'cannot be cured within 120 days', substitution only within 180 days of the Closing Date — and the deemed-materiality parenthetical and 'sole remedies' sentence are both heavily loaded.","reasoning_cat2":"The indemnity is expressly conditioned on the loans 'not [being] the subject of a Reconstitution', yet the whole deal contemplates exactly one Reconstitution under Section 12, and Section 13 declares the Purchaser's remedies 'cumulative', contradicting 'sole remedies'.","prob_cat1":0.52,"prob_cat2":0.58},

{"clause_id":"c253","reasoning_cat1":"It repeatedly refers to 'each Closing Date' although a single Closing Date is defined, and the enumerated conditions are typographically scrambled with (iv) and (v) detached from their text.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 10 likewise assumes multiple Closing Dates ('to be executed and delivered only for the initial Closing Date'), suggesting the form contemplated flow purchases that this single-closing deal does not.","prob_cat1":0.29,"prob_cat2":0.30},
{"clause_id":"c254","reasoning_cat1":"The list numbering collapses after item '1.', so the five documents are not separately identified in the text as it stands.","reasoning_cat2":"It requires delivery of the Letter Agreement, an agreement between two non-parties, as a closing document.","prob_cat1":0.26,"prob_cat2":0.22},
{"clause_id":"c255","reasoning_cat1":"A specific seller list followed by 'All other costs and expenses ... including, without limitation' allocated to the Purchaser — an enumerated/catch-all pairing.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 24 puts recordation costs on the Seller 'in the event recordation is either necessary ... or requested by the Purchaser', which is consistent with this allocation.","prob_cat1":0.19,"prob_cat2":0.19},
{"clause_id":"c256","reasoning_cat1":"Long and multi-part; 'reasonable best efforts', 'as if it were the related Originator' and the indemnity's clarification proviso are all soft or convoluted, though individually legible.","reasoning_cat2":"It limits the Purchaser to 'one (1) Reconstitution' while Section 18 says the Purchaser 'shall be limited to three (3) assignments or transfers with respect to the Mortgage Loans and this Agreement as described in Section 12' — a direct numerical conflict.","prob_cat1":0.32,"prob_cat2":0.55},
{"clause_id":"c257","reasoning_cat1":"It grants a security interest in loans the Seller has just sold outright and speaks of the Purchaser's 'obligation to pay the Purchase Price' as if unpaid; the final sentence makes all remedies cumulative.","reasoning_cat2":"The cumulative-remedies sentence cannot easily stand with Subsection 8.02's statement that cure, substitution, repurchase and indemnity 'constitute the sole remedies of the Purchaser', nor with Subsection 6.02's outright sale.","prob_cat1":0.28,"prob_cat2":0.50},
{"clause_id":"c258","reasoning_cat1":"The Purchaser's notice block names an individual and an address but never names EMC Mortgage Corporation, and notice is deemed given 'if mailed' rather than on receipt for mailed notices.","reasoning_cat2":"The principal agreement gives EMC's fax at the same address as a differently transcribed number, and Section 19's writing requirement fits this clause without conflict.","prob_cat1":0.22,"prob_cat2":0.16}

{"clause_id":"c223","reasoning_cat1":"The trailing qualifier 'none of which is a mobile home' is ambiguous as to whether it modifies only Manufactured Homes or all six enumerated categories.","reasoning_cat2":"The Manufactured Home definition describes a transportable factory-built unit, making the mobile-home exclusion harder to apply consistently.","prob_cat1":0.28,"prob_cat2":0.18},
{"clause_id":"c224","reasoning_cat1":"Bare entity definition.","reasoning_cat2":"Used in Section 7 and Exhibit C/E consistently.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c225","reasoning_cat1":"One-line definition; nothing ambiguous in itself.","reasoning_cat2":"It refers to 'a second lien Mortgage', but the Mortgage definition says a Mortgage is an instrument 'which creates a first lien on the Mortgaged Property' — the two cannot both be right.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.38},
{"clause_id":"c226","reasoning_cat1":"Two broad but structured limbs covering both direct transfers and payment-linked issuances.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 12's Reconstitution machinery and the Letter Agreement's reference to a 'proposed Securitization Transaction'.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.10},
{"clause_id":"c227","reasoning_cat1":"Specific to co-op collateral; clear.","reasoning_cat2":"Dovetails with the Mortgage definition's treatment of Co-op Loans.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c228","reasoning_cat1":"Pointer to the initial paragraph plus successors and assigns.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent; note Section 18 restricts the Seller's ability to assign, which the 'and assigns' tail does not undo.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.12},
{"clause_id":"c229","reasoning_cat1":"Uses a period rather than a colon after the term, a typographical slip only.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 12 does define Seller Information by reference to specified Regulation AB items; accurate.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.09},
{"clause_id":"c230","reasoning_cat1":"Defines the Servicer only by reference to a schedule.","reasoning_cat2":"Exhibit B is a placeholder page ('Provided Upon Request') and Section 7 refers to 'the Mortgage Loan Schedule attached as Exhibit C hereto', which is the Prior Purchase/Servicing Agreements exhibit, so the exhibit references do not line up.","prob_cat1":0.12,"prob_cat2":0.31},
{"clause_id":"c231","reasoning_cat1":"Defines the term by reference to Exhibit C, which does list the servicing agreements.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 7's reference to 'the Mortgage Loan Schedule attached as Exhibit C' conflates the Schedule (Exhibit B) with the agreements list (Exhibit C).","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.28},
{"clause_id":"c232","reasoning_cat1":"Short and derivative of the Servicing Agreements; clear.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 4's netting of Servicing Fees and Subsection 8.02's remittance mechanics.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c233","reasoning_cat1":"A seven-limb list with sweeping catch-alls ('all accounts and other rights to payment related to any of the property described in this paragraph').","reasoning_cat2":"The Seller reserves Servicing Rights under Subsection 6.01, yet Section 7 says the loans are sold 'servicing retained' while the Servicing Agreements are assigned to the Purchaser and Saxon holds some rights — the pieces are hard to align.","prob_cat1":0.26,"prob_cat2":0.34},
{"clause_id":"c234","reasoning_cat1":"'the principal balance ... at the Cut-off Date after giving effect to payments of principal due on or before such date' leaves 'such date' ambiguous between the Cut-off Date and the date of determination.","reasoning_cat2":"Stated Principal Balance drives both the Purchase Price in Section 4 and the Repurchase Price, so the ambiguity has real consequences.","prob_cat1":0.29,"prob_cat2":0.23},
{"clause_id":"c235","reasoning_cat1":"A single sentence stating the sale, its servicing-retained basis and the balance 'set forth on the Mortgage Loan Schedule'; clear on its face.","reasoning_cat2":"The Schedule (Exhibit B) is a blank placeholder, so the quantity sold is not ascertainable from the instrument, and Section 7's servicing arrangements complicate 'servicing retained'.","prob_cat1":0.15,"prob_cat2":0.30},
{"clause_id":"c236","reasoning_cat1":"A concrete delivery deadline with a reasonable-time proviso for Purchaser-caused changes.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 9(i) also requires preparation of 'a complete Mortgage Loan Schedule' before closing; the two obligations coexist.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c237","reasoning_cat1":"The formula is clear, but the entitlement paragraph mixes a Cut-off Date test for principal with a Closing Date test for interest without explaining the gap.","reasoning_cat2":"The Closing Date (May 31, 2007) precedes the Cut-off Date (June 1, 2007), so interest accrues to the Purchaser from before the date used to measure principal, an ordering that is hard to harmonise.","prob_cat1":0.26,"prob_cat2":0.38},
{"clause_id":"c238","reasoning_cat1":"Clear examination provision preserving repurchase and substitution rights regardless of review.","reasoning_cat2":"Parallel to Section 5 of the principal agreement and consistent with Subsection 8.02's remedies.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.12},
{"clause_id":"c239","reasoning_cat1":"Conveyance language is standard, but it takes effect 'simultaneously with the execution and delivery of this Agreement' (May 1) even though title and payment are keyed to the Closing Date.","reasoning_cat2":"The carve-out of Group 1 Mortgage Loans from the Prior Purchase Agreement assignment is the hinge for Subsection 8.02's split between assigned Originator reps and the Seller's own Part A reps, and Subsection 6.02 says record title stays with the Seller.","prob_cat1":0.26,"prob_cat2":0.38},
{"clause_id":"c240","reasoning_cat1":"The final sentence is corrupted ('and a asa a sale of assets 0 on the') and simply stops, so the sale-treatment covenant is incomplete.","reasoning_cat2":"It also holds record title in the Seller while vesting ownership in the Purchaser, which must be read with Section 13's security interest and Section 17's intention clause.","prob_cat1":0.40,"prob_cat2":0.30},
{"clause_id":"c241","reasoning_cat1":"Clear sequence of custodian certifications, authorisation and fee shifting.","reasoning_cat2":"Mortgage Loan Documents are defined as the documents required 'pursuant to Subsection 6.03', which itself points to Exhibit A-1, a workable but circular chain.","prob_cat1":0.12,"prob_cat2":0.20},
{"clause_id":"c242","reasoning_cat1":"Three concrete MERS designations; nothing ambiguous.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the MERS Designated Mortgage Loan, Investor and Interim Funder definitions.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.09},
{"clause_id":"c243","reasoning_cat1":"It states the loans were sold 'servicing retained' and then assigns every Servicing Agreement to the Purchaser with the Servicers servicing 'for the Purchaser', which is in tension with the retained-servicing label.","reasoning_cat2":"It refers to 'the Mortgage Loan Schedule attached as Exhibit C hereto' when the Schedule is Exhibit B and Exhibit C holds the agreements, and Subsection 6.01 excepts the Servicing Rights from the conveyance.","prob_cat1":0.35,"prob_cat2":0.42},
{"clause_id":"c244","reasoning_cat1":"Long but conventional authority rep with standard enforceability carve-outs.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 10's closing documents and the Assignment and Assumption Agreement's parallel rep.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c245","reasoning_cat1":"The sentence contains a duplicated verb ('No consent ... is required for the transactions ... having jurisdiction over the Seller is required'), leaving the syntax broken.","reasoning_cat2":"The same garbled formulation is reproduced in paragraph (h) of the Assignment and Assumption Agreement, so it is a copied defect rather than a conflict.","prob_cat1":0.33,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c246","reasoning_cat1":"'The consummation of the transactions ... are' is a subject-verb slip, and 'ordinary course of business' is an evaluative standard.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the sale-treatment provisions in Subsections 6.02 and 8.01(g).","prob_cat1":0.17,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c247","reasoning_cat1":"Notably narrow — it tests conflicts only against the Seller's charter and by-laws, not against law or other agreements — but the words are clear.","reasoning_cat2":"Its narrowness contrasts with the corresponding reps in the principal agreement, which extend to law and orders; that is a difference in scope, not a contradiction.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c248","reasoning_cat1":"Standard no-litigation rep bounded by knowledge and by materiality of impairment.","reasoning_cat2":"Mirrored in the Assignment and Assumption Agreement paragraph (i); consistent.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c249","reasoning_cat1":"'does not believe, nor does it have any reason or cause to believe, that it cannot perform' is a double-negative, wholly subjective formulation whose content is hard to pin down.","reasoning_cat2":"It overlaps the more objective authority and enforceability reps in 8.01(a) without conflicting with them.","prob_cat1":0.30,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c250","reasoning_cat1":"A short, concrete accounting and tax covenant.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Subsection 6.02's sale intention and Section 17's tax characterisation.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c251","reasoning_cat1":"Several timing rules pull against each other — action 'within 120 days' of discovery, repurchase if the breach 'cannot be cured within 120 days', substitution only within 180 days of the Closing Date — and the deemed-materiality parenthetical and 'sole remedies' sentence are both heavily loaded.","reasoning_cat2":"The indemnity is expressly conditioned on the loans 'not [being] the subject of a Reconstitution', yet the whole deal contemplates exactly one Reconstitution under Section 12, and Section 13 declares the Purchaser's remedies 'cumulative', contradicting 'sole remedies'.","prob_cat1":0.52,"prob_cat2":0.58},
{"clause_id":"c252","reasoning_cat1":"It defines the Seller's duty by reference to remedial actions 'described in the related Prior Purchase Agreement' rather than stating them, and packs several dated conditions into one long sentence.","reasoning_cat2":"The second paragraph makes repurchase turn on whether a loan 'is not the subject of a Reconstitution', which interacts awkwardly with Section 12's single permitted Reconstitution and with Subsection 8.02's indemnity carve-out.","prob_cat1":0.27,"prob_cat2":0.33},
{"clause_id":"c253","reasoning_cat1":"It repeatedly refers to 'each Closing Date' although a single Closing Date is defined, and the enumerated conditions are typographically scrambled with (iv) and (v) detached from their text.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 10 likewise assumes multiple Closing Dates ('to be executed and delivered only for the initial Closing Date'), suggesting the form contemplated flow purchases that this single-closing deal does not.","prob_cat1":0.29,"prob_cat2":0.30},
{"clause_id":"c254","reasoning_cat1":"The list numbering collapses after item '1.', so the five documents are not separately identified in the text as it stands.","reasoning_cat2":"It requires delivery of the Letter Agreement, an agreement between two non-parties, as a closing document.","prob_cat1":0.26,"prob_cat2":0.22},
{"clause_id":"c255","reasoning_cat1":"A specific seller list followed by 'All other costs and expenses ... including, without limitation' allocated to the Purchaser — an enumerated/catch-all pairing.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 24 puts recordation costs on the Seller 'in the event recordation is either necessary ... or requested by the Purchaser', which is consistent with this allocation.","prob_cat1":0.19,"prob_cat2":0.19},
{"clause_id":"c256","reasoning_cat1":"Long and multi-part; 'reasonable best efforts', 'as if it were the related Originator' and the indemnity's clarification proviso are all soft or convoluted, though individually legible.","reasoning_cat2":"It limits the Purchaser to 'one (1) Reconstitution' while Section 18 says the Purchaser 'shall be limited to three (3) assignments or transfers with respect to the Mortgage Loans and this Agreement as described in Section 12' — a direct numerical conflict.","prob_cat1":0.32,"prob_cat2":0.55},
{"clause_id":"c257","reasoning_cat1":"It grants a security interest in loans the Seller has just sold outright and speaks of the Purchaser's 'obligation to pay the Purchase Price' as if unpaid; the final sentence makes all remedies cumulative.","reasoning_cat2":"The cumulative-remedies sentence cannot easily stand with Subsection 8.02's statement that cure, substitution, repurchase and indemnity 'constitute the sole remedies of the Purchaser', nor with Subsection 6.02's outright sale.","prob_cat1":0.28,"prob_cat2":0.50},
{"clause_id":"c258","reasoning_cat1":"The Purchaser's notice block names an individual and an address but never names EMC Mortgage Corporation, and notice is deemed given 'if mailed' rather than on receipt for mailed notices.","reasoning_cat2":"The principal agreement gives EMC's fax at the same address as a differently transcribed number, and Section 19's writing requirement fits this clause without conflict.","prob_cat1":0.22,"prob_cat2":0.16}
]}

{"judgments": [
{"clause_id":"c259","reasoning_cat1":"'Any part, provision representation or warranty' is missing a comma and 'nearly as possible the same' is garbled, but the operation of the clause is clear.","reasoning_cat2":"The good-faith renegotiation duty in the last sentence coexists with Section 19's writing requirement for modifications; no conflict identified.","prob_cat1":0.21,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c260","reasoning_cat1":"Standard counterparts clause; nothing to construe.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the separately executed signature pages.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c261","reasoning_cat1":"Clear statement of sale and tax intent with a grantor-trust fallback; the fallback is contingent but comprehensible.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Subsections 6.02 and 8.01(g), though it sits alongside Section 13's grant of a security interest in the same loans.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.22},
{"clause_id":"c262","reasoning_cat1":"'The Purchaser shall be limited to three (3) assignments or transfers with respect to the Mortgage Loans and this Agreement as described in Section 12' is ambiguous as to whether the cap counts Reconstitutions, assignments, or both.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 12 states the Purchaser 'shall be limited to one (1) Reconstitution', so the two limits on the same activity are numerically irreconcilable.","prob_cat1":0.29,"prob_cat2":0.54},
{"clause_id":"c263","reasoning_cat1":"Short, standard no-oral-waiver clause.","reasoning_cat2":"Mirrored in Exhibit D paragraph 4; consistent.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c264","reasoning_cat1":"One line incorporating the exhibits; nothing to construe.","reasoning_cat2":"Several exhibits (B, and the Exhibit D sub-exhibits) are blank placeholders, which makes 'integral part' do more work than it easily can.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.23},
{"clause_id":"c265","reasoning_cat1":"Standard interpretive canons; paragraph (f) expressly disables ejusdem generis for 'include', which is itself a construction rule rather than an ambiguity.","reasoning_cat2":"It governs the many enumerated lists in Section 8 and Exhibit F, resolving rather than creating tension.","prob_cat1":0.12,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c266","reasoning_cat1":"Detailed and self-contained evidentiary clause.","reasoning_cat2":"No other provision addresses reproductions; no conflict.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c267","reasoning_cat1":"Short further-assurances clause bounded by reasonableness.","reasoning_cat2":"Overlaps Section 12's cooperation duties without contradicting them.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c268","reasoning_cat1":"'is subject to recordation ... in any other appropriate public recording office or elsewhere' is loose, and 'requested by the Purchaser at its sole option' gives an unbounded trigger for Seller-funded recording.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 11 already allocates recordation fees to the Seller, and Exhibit A-1(e) says assignments need be recorded only where necessary or customary — three provisions on the same subject that must be harmonised.","prob_cat1":0.20,"prob_cat2":0.26},
{"clause_id":"c269","reasoning_cat1":"Carve-out (i) reads 'so long as such promotional material either is sent to the mortgagors for all of the mortgages ...' with no matching 'or', so the condition is incomplete on its face.","reasoning_cat2":"The final paragraph excluding general-public promotions fits the carve-outs; the defect is internal to the clause rather than a conflict.","prob_cat1":0.41,"prob_cat2":0.16},
{"clause_id":"c270","reasoning_cat1":"Standard mutual jury waiver; nothing to construe.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Section 27 forum clause.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c271","reasoning_cat1":"Comprehensive choice of law, forum and service clause; the drafting is conventional despite OCR mangling of the roman numerals.","reasoning_cat2":"Its statement that the Agreement is 'deemed in effect when a fully executed counterpart ... is received by the Purchaser' sits slightly awkwardly with Subsection 6.01's conveyance 'simultaneously with the execution and delivery'.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.20},
{"clause_id":"c272","reasoning_cat1":"Short compliance covenant tied to a named statute; 'designed to protect' is a soft standard but conventional.","reasoning_cat2":"No other provision addresses borrower privacy; no conflict.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c273","reasoning_cat1":"'available for inspection by the Purchaser and any prospective Purchaser' extends inspection to undefined third parties.","reasoning_cat2":"It says delivery is 'pursuant to Section 6', and Subsection 6.03 in fact leaves the documents with the Custodians rather than delivering them, so the exhibit and section describe different mechanics.","prob_cat1":0.17,"prob_cat2":0.26},
{"clause_id":"c274","reasoning_cat1":"The required endorsement is quoted with a blank ('Pay to the order of , without recourse'), leaving unclear whether endorsement is to be in blank or to a named endorsee.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 4(b) of the principal agreement contemplates delivery of Mortgage Notes to the Trustee, and Subsection 8.02 requires the Note 'endorsed as required by Subsection 6.03', so the blank matters downstream.","prob_cat1":0.31,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c275","reasoning_cat1":"One line, clear alternative of original or imaged copy.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the rest of Exhibit A-1's imaged-copy regime.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c276","reasoning_cat1":"Long but structured; it permits 'the original or an imaged copy' as equally acceptable, which is unusual but stated plainly.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 4(b) of the principal agreement requires originals or certified true copies with specific certifications, a stricter regime for the same documents.","prob_cat1":0.21,"prob_cat2":0.27},
{"clause_id":"c277","reasoning_cat1":"Short and specific.","reasoning_cat2":"Fits Exhibit F Part A(Q) on unmodified terms; consistent.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c278","reasoning_cat1":"'commonly required by private institutional mortgage investors in the area' is a vague trigger for recording, and the parenthetical uses 'MERS Designated Loan', a variant of the defined term.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 24 makes recordation turn on necessity or Purchaser request, and Subsection 6.04 handles MERS loans, so three provisions state overlapping and slightly different recording triggers.","prob_cat1":0.34,"prob_cat2":0.30},
{"clause_id":"c279","reasoning_cat1":"It requires a chain of assignment 'from the Seller to the Last Endorsee', which reverses the natural direction (the Seller should be the last link), and the sentence runs to great length.","reasoning_cat2":"Exhibit A-1(a) defines the Last Endorsee as the last endorsee on the Note, so the two exhibits describe the chain inconsistently.","prob_cat1":0.31,"prob_cat2":0.26},

{"clause_id":"c282","reasoning_cat1":"'imaged copies of the (i) the Co-op Lease' duplicates the article, but the four enumerated items are specific.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Co-op, Co-op Lease, Security Agreement and Co-op UCC Filing definitions.","prob_cat1":0.17,"prob_cat2":0.11},
